Name: Deaccelerationist
Description: Informal label for a stance favoring slower technological development or deployment, especially of AI, to address perceived risks. The label has no single standardized policy program.

Name: Pro-online safety
Description: Supports measures to reduce harms associated with online services, such as abuse, exploitation, or harmful platform design. Specific approaches to moderation, privacy, and age verification vary.

Name: Pro-deregulation
Description: Favors reducing or simplifying government rules on businesses and markets.

Name: Pro-regulation
Description: Favors government rules and oversight to address market failures, protect the public, or constrain harmful conduct.

Name: Pro-court reform
Description: Supports changes to courts' structure, procedures, appointments, or ethics rules. Support for reform does not by itself specify a particular proposal or constitutional interpretation.

Name: Pro-criminal justice reform
Description: Supports changes to policing, courts, sentencing, or incarceration intended to improve fairness or outcomes.

Name: Pro-school choice
Description: Supports families having options beyond their assigned public school, including other public schools, charter schools, private schools, or homeschooling; funding preferences vary.

Name: Dove
Description: Favors restraint in using military force and prefers diplomacy or limited commitments.

Name: Pro Iran containment
Description: Favors limiting Iran’s regional influence through deterrence, sanctions, or other pressure.

Name: Free trader
Description: Favors reducing barriers to international trade and maintaining open trade relationships.

Name: Pro-welfare expansion
Description: Supports expanding public benefits or social programs that provide income, health, or other assistance.

Name: Crypto skeptic
Description: Questions the benefits or safety of cryptocurrencies and favors caution or stronger safeguards.

Name: Pro-market wages
Description: Favors wages being determined primarily through labor-market bargaining rather than statutory wage floors or government-mandated increases.

Name: Pro-judicial independence
Description: Supports courts and judges deciding cases impartially, free from improper interference or pressure. Judicial independence can coexist with court reform and accountability.

Name: Pro-Taiwan defense
Description: Supports military assistance, deterrence, or defensive commitments intended to protect Taiwan against attack or coercion. This does not by itself imply support for a formal declaration of independence.

Name: Gender-critical
Description: Holds that biological sex is distinct from gender identity and should remain a basis for relevant legal and social distinctions. Specific policy positions vary.

Name: NATO skeptic
Description: Questions NATO’s purpose, costs, expansion, or members’ obligations.

Name: Climate skeptic
Description: Umbrella label for views questioning aspects of climate-change science, projected impacts, or proposed responses. Skepticism about a particular policy does not necessarily imply rejection of human-caused warming.

Name: Pro-LGBTQ rights
Description: Supports equal legal rights and protections for LGBTQ people.

Name: Pro-vaccination
Description: Supports vaccination as a means of preventing disease and protecting health. Support for vaccination does not by itself imply support for vaccine mandates.

Name: Pro-NATO
Description: Supports the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and its role in collective defense and security cooperation among its members.

Name: Pro legalization
Description: Supports making specified currently prohibited drugs or related activities lawful under a legal framework. Legalization is distinct from only removing criminal penalties for possession or use.

Name: Church-state separationist
Description: Supports keeping government institutions and religious institutions legally separate.

Name: Protectionist
Description: Supports trade barriers or domestic preferences intended to protect local industries and workers from foreign competition.

Name: Pro-living wage
Description: Supports pay sufficient to afford a decent standard of living for workers and their families. This can be pursued through wage-setting policies, collective bargaining, or employer practices.

Name: Pro-foreign aid
Description: Supports providing assistance to other countries for purposes such as humanitarian relief, development, or security. Support is not limited to one agency or aid program.

Name: Pro-AI acceleration
Description: Supports faster development and deployment of artificial intelligence. Views on appropriate safety measures and regulation vary.

Name: Pro-Palestinian
Description: Supports Palestinian rights, interests, or political self-determination.

Name: Neighborhood preservation
Description: Favors protecting the character or stability of existing residential neighborhoods, often through local land-use controls.

Name: Pro-nuclear power
Description: Supports using or expanding nuclear energy to generate electricity.

Name: Progressive taxation
Description: Supports tax structures in which higher-income taxpayers pay a larger proportion of their income in tax than lower-income taxpayers.

Name: Pro-welfare reform
Description: Supports changes to public assistance programs' design, eligibility, administration, or incentives. The label alone does not establish whether benefits would expand or contract.

Name: Pro-immigration
Description: Supports immigration or policies that make immigration and immigrant integration easier.

Name: Pro-Ukraine
Description: Supports Ukraine’s sovereignty and its defense against Russia’s invasion.

Name: Pro-entitlement reform
Description: Supports changes to statutory benefit programs, such as Social Security or Medicare, to alter their financing, eligibility, or benefits. Proposals may expand or reduce particular benefits.

Name: Pro-repayment
Description: Favors borrowers repaying student loans and opposes or limits loan cancellation.

Name: Pro-public spending
Description: Supports government spending on public programs, services, or investment.

Name: Pro-Israel
Description: Supports Israel's security, national interests, or continued existence as a Jewish state. The label does not necessarily imply support for every Israeli government policy.

Name: Pro-election integrity
Description: Supports measures intended to ensure elections are accurate, secure, lawful, and fairly administered. Specific measures and their effects on voting access are matters of debate.

Name: Anti-nuclear
Description: Opposes nuclear power or its expansion.

Name: Pro-gun control
Description: Supports laws that restrict or regulate access to firearms.

Name: Pro-gun rights
Description: Supports legal protections for firearm ownership and use. Views on which restrictions are acceptable vary.

Name: Pro internet freedom
Description: Supports freedom of expression, access to information, and participation online, with limits on censorship and unjustified restrictions.

Name: Pro-climate action
Description: Supports public or private measures to reduce climate change or adapt to its effects.

Name: Pro-states' rights
Description: Supports state governments’ authority relative to the federal government.

Name: Pro-fossil fuels
Description: Supports continued or expanded production and use of fossil fuels, including coal, oil, and natural gas.

Name: Social conservative
Description: Political outlook favoring traditional social institutions and moral norms, especially concerning family, religion, sexuality, and gender.

Name: Pro- universal healthcare
Description: Supports ensuring that everyone can obtain needed health services without financial hardship. Universal coverage can involve public, private, or mixed systems.

Name: Pro-innovation
Description: Supports policies or practices that encourage the development and adoption of new ideas, technologies, products, or processes.

Name: Pro-China engagement
Description: Supports diplomacy, trade, or cooperation with China rather than isolating or confronting it.

Name: Pro-voting rights
Description: Supports protecting or expanding access to voting and participation in elections.

Name: Fiscal hawk
Description: Favors limiting deficits and public debt through spending discipline, revenue, or both.

Name: Pro-federal authority
Description: Supports federal government authority over states in areas assigned to or best handled by the national government.

Name: Pro-border security
Description: Supports stronger enforcement and security measures at national borders.

Name: Pro-Iran diplomacy
Description: Supports negotiating with Iran and using diplomacy to manage disputes or reduce conflict.

Name: Pro-law enforcement
Description: Supports police and other law-enforcement agencies, their capacity, or their role in public safety.

Name: Pro-vaccine choice
Description: Supports individual choice about vaccination and opposes vaccine mandates.

Name: Pro-clean energy
Description: Supports energy sources with lower greenhouse-gas emissions, such as renewables or nuclear power.

Name: Pro-meritocracy
Description: Supports allocating opportunities, responsibilities, or rewards according to relevant ability, effort, and achievement. Views on how merit should be measured and unequal starting conditions addressed vary.

Name: Pro-equity
Description: Supports addressing unjust disadvantages and barriers to fair treatment or opportunities. The term's application to resources, procedures, and outcomes varies by context.

Name: Pro-religious freedom
Description: Supports the right to practice religion and protections for religious belief and exercise.

Name: Pro-housing development
Description: Supports building more housing or reducing barriers to new residential construction.

Name: Pro-foreign aid reform
Description: Supports changes to foreign assistance programs' objectives, allocation, delivery, or oversight. Reform may involve expansion, reduction, or redirection of particular programs.

Name: Pro-death penalty
Description: Supports retaining or applying capital punishment for certain serious crimes.

Name: Benefit preservation
Description: Supports maintaining existing public benefits or protecting recipients against benefit reductions, including in programs such as Social Security.

Name: Ukraine aid skeptic
Description: Questions the scale, duration, effectiveness, or conditions of assistance to Ukraine and may favor limiting or conditioning it. This stance does not by itself establish support for Russia.

Name: Prohibitionist
Description: In this dataset's drug-policy context, supports legal prohibitions on specified drugs or drug-related activities and opposes their legalization.

Name: Pro-tax cuts
Description: Supports reducing tax rates or the amount of tax people or businesses pay.
Slogan: Read my lips: no new taxes

Name: Pro-surveillance
Description: Supports using or expanding surveillance powers for purposes such as intelligence gathering, law enforcement, or security. Views on authorization, oversight, and privacy safeguards vary.

Name: Pro-transgender rights
Description: Supports equal legal rights and protections for transgender people.

Name: Pro-life
Description: Opposes abortion, especially on the grounds that fetal life should receive legal protection.

Name: Death penalty abolitionist
Description: Supports ending capital punishment.

Name: Pro-choice
Description: Supports legal access to abortion and the right to decide whether to continue a pregnancy.

Name: Pro-union
Description: Supports labor unions and collective bargaining rights for workers.

Name: Pro-public education
Description: Supports public schools and public investment in education.

Name: Hawk
Description: Favors a more forceful foreign policy and is comparatively willing to use military power.

Name: Pro-Taiwan restraint
Description: Favors limiting U.S. military commitments or escalation risks concerning Taiwan and prioritizing diplomacy or other nonmilitary approaches. This does not by itself imply support for unification with China.

Name: Pro-China containment
Description: Favors limiting China’s power or influence through deterrence, alliances, or other pressure.

Name: Pro-privacy
Description: Supports protecting personal information and limiting unwarranted data collection or surveillance.

Name: Anti-union
Description: Opposes labor unions or supports restricting their power, membership, or collective bargaining.

Name: Free-market healthcare
Description: Supports a greater role for market competition, private provision, and consumer choice in healthcare. Specific views on public financing, regulation, and assistance vary.

Name: Pro-crypto
Description: Supports cryptocurrencies and policies that enable their use or growth.

Name: Pro-AI regulation
Description: Supports rules or oversight governing the development or use of artificial intelligence.

Name: Pro-student debt relief
Description: Supports reducing or cancelling student loan debt for borrowers.

Name: Techno-optimist
Description: Broad outlook expecting technological development to produce substantial benefits for human well-being. It does not by itself imply support for every technology or for removing all regulation.

Name: Anti zionist
Description: Opposes Zionism as a political ideology or movement supporting Jewish national self-determination in Israel. Anti-Zionist positions vary and extend beyond criticism of particular Israeli government policies.

Name: Classical liberal
Description: Political philosophy emphasizing individual liberty, civil liberties, private property, the rule of law, and limits on government power; views on the state's economic role vary.

Name: Nationalist
Description: Political outlook that gives special importance to national identity and self-government and prioritizes the nation's interests. Nationalist traditions differ on citizenship, ethnicity, and international cooperation.

Name: Globalist
Description: Political outlook favoring international integration and cooperation in economic and foreign affairs. The label has several meanings and is also used pejoratively.

Name: Secularist
Description: Political outlook favoring state neutrality toward religion and belief and limits on religious authority over government. Secularism does not require individuals to be nonreligious.

Name: Conservative
Description: Political tradition valuing inherited institutions, customs, and social continuity and generally favoring cautious change. Its policies and understanding of tradition vary across countries and periods.

Name: Paleoconservative
Description: A U.S. conservative current emphasizing national sovereignty, cultural tradition, restrictive immigration, and restraint in foreign intervention.

Name: MAGA
Description: Political movement and associated nationalist-populist outlook centered on Donald Trump's Make America Great Again slogan, emphasizing America First policies, immigration restrictions, and opposition to political elites.

Name: Democratic socialist
Description: Socialist outlook combining political democracy with social ownership and democratic control of economic life. It is distinct from policies that solely regulate capitalism or expand welfare.

Name: Liberal
Description: In contemporary U.S. politics, an outlook supporting civil liberties, equal rights, and government action to address social and economic inequalities. Liberalism has broader and differing meanings internationally.

Name: Socialist
Description: Family of political and economic views favoring social ownership or democratic control of productive resources rather than their predominantly private ownership. Socialist traditions differ on markets, planning, and political strategy.

Name: Feminist
Description: Family of social and political perspectives seeking equality for women and challenging sex- and gender-based subordination. Feminist traditions differ in their explanations of inequality and proposed remedies.

Name: Marxist
Description: Social and political outlook drawing on Karl Marx's analysis of class relations, historical change, and capitalism, including its critique of exploitation and class domination.

Name: Neoconservative
Description: A conservative outlook associated with an assertive U.S. foreign policy, military strength, and support for promoting democracy abroad.

Name: Communist
Description: Political ideology seeking a classless society based on common ownership of productive resources. Communist traditions differ over how to achieve that goal and the role of the state.

Name: Social democrat
Description: In its contemporary sense, a political tradition supporting a predominantly market economy alongside democratic government, economic regulation, labor protections, and extensive public services and social welfare.

Name: Humanist
Description: Ethical and philosophical worldview emphasizing human dignity, reason, and human welfare. Broader than a specifically political ideology, humanism includes both religious and nonreligious traditions.

Name: Traditionalist
Description: An outlook that values inherited customs and institutions and favors preserving social continuity over rapid change.

Name: Neoliberal
Description: Contested label for political and economic ideas emphasizing markets, private enterprise, and competition, often associated with privatization, deregulation, and trade liberalization; views on welfare and state institutions vary.

Name: Populist
Description: Political outlook presenting society as divided between the people and a corrupt elite and demanding that politics express the people's will. It can combine with left-wing or right-wing ideologies.

Name: Libertarian
Description: Political outlook giving individual liberty priority and opposing coercive interference. In contemporary U.S. usage, it commonly combines strong private-property rights and market freedom with civil liberties.

Name: Islamist
Description: Family of political outlooks seeking to organize government and public life according to interpretations of Islamic principles. Islamist movements differ substantially and should not be equated with Islam or Muslim identity.

Name: Environmentalist
Description: Broad social and political outlook placing protection of the natural environment at the center of public concerns, including conservation, pollution prevention, and ecological sustainability.

Name: Progressive
Description: A U.S. political outlook supporting reforms or structural changes to expand social and economic equality, civil rights, and environmental protection.

Name: Libertarianism
Description: Family of political philosophies giving individual liberty priority and imposing stringent limits on coercion. Libertarian traditions differ on property, redistribution, and whether any state is justified.

Name: Christian conservative
Description: Conservative political outlook informed by Christian beliefs and moral traditions, often emphasizing religion's public role and traditional views on family, marriage, and abortion.

Name: Isolationist
Description: Foreign-policy outlook favoring avoidance of foreign wars and binding political or military commitments. It is distinct from simply opposing one intervention and need not mean ending all international trade.

Name: Anarchist
Description: A political outlook opposing the state and other coercive hierarchies and favoring voluntary association and self-governance. Anarchist traditions differ widely on property, markets, and social organization.
